metadata.title: fix: honor fail_on_plugin_error during plugin init
metadata.author: lucarlig

description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

Before opening this PR please:

1. `make lint`            - passes `ruff`, `mypy`, `pylint`
2. `make test`            - all unit + integration tests green
3. `make coverage`        - ≥ 80 %
4. `make docker docker-run-ssl` or `make podman podman-run-ssl`
5. Update relevant documentation.
6. Tested with sqlite and postgres + redis.
7. Manual regression no longer fails. Ensure the UI and /version work correctly.

---

## 📌 Summary
Honor `plugin_settings.fail_on_plugin_error` during plugin-manager startup so an unavailable external plugin can be skipped instead of aborting gateway boot. Add a regression test that locks the fail-open startup behavior in place.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
Closes #4033

1. Enable plugins with `plugin_settings.fail_on_plugin_error: false`.
2. Configure an external MCP plugin whose streamable HTTP endpoint is unavailable at startup.
3. Start the gateway.
4. Observe that startup aborts from `PluginManager.initialize()` instead of logging and skipping the failing plugin.

## 🐞 Root Cause
`PluginManager.initialize()` unconditionally raised `RuntimeError` on plugin instantiation failures, even when config explicitly requested fail-open behavior via `fail_on_plugin_error: false`.

## 💡 Fix Description
Check `plugin_settings.fail_on_plugin_error` inside the plugin-load failure path during manager initialization. When it is `false`, log the failure, skip the plugin, and continue startup. Add a unit regression test that patches `load_and_instantiate_plugin()` to raise and asserts initialization still completes with an empty registry.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                                 | Command                                                                  | Status |
|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| Lint suite                            | `make lint`                                                              | Not run |
| Unit tests                            | `uv run pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/plugins/framework/test_manager.py tests/unit/mcpgateway/plugins/framework/test_manager_extended.py -q` | Passed |
| Coverage ≥ 80 %                       | `make coverage`                                                          | Not run |

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

reviews.author: madhu-mohan-jaishankar
reviews.body: `logger.warning` message for the skip behavior should be asserted.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Rebased onto main (was 6 commits behind) — clean, no conflicts.

**Code review:**

- Logic is correct and minimal: the 3-line addition checks `fail_on_plugin_error` before raising, logs a warning, and `continue`s to the next plugin. Clean fix.
- The `self._config` null guard is consistent with the runtime checks in `execute_plugin()` (lines 388/400/404).
- The existing `test_manager_initialization_edge_cases` was correctly updated to set `fail_on_plugin_error=True` explicitly — previously relied on the unconditional raise, so it needs the explicit flag now.
- New test covers the skip path with the right assertions (warning logged, init completes, plugin count is 0).
- 100% differential coverage confirmed — lines 823-825 are all covered.
- No security or performance concerns. The skip is gated behind an explicit opt-in setting, and failures are logged at both ERROR and WARNING levels.

**One minor design note** (non-blocking): The runtime error handling in `execute_plugin()` also raises for `PluginMode.ENFORCE` regardless of `fail_on_plugin_error`. The init path only checks `fail_on_plugin_error`. This is reasonable since at init time there's no request to enforce against, and the admin has explicitly opted into fail-open. Worth considering as a follow-up if stricter init behavior is desired for ENFORCE-mode plugins.

LGTM — nice clean fix, Luca.
